scenes.headline: Writing Data
scenes.subtitle: Persisting DataFrames back to storage.
scenes.narration: Writing data saves a DataFrame back to durable storage in a chosen format, completing the pipeline.

scenes.headline: The writer API
items: df.write is the entry point for saving
Choose a format like parquet, csv, or json
Save mode controls overwrite, append, or error
Partitioning organizes output for faster future reads
scenes.narration: The df.write object is the entry point for saving. You pick a format such as Parquet, choose a save mode that controls overwrite or append behavior, and can partition the output to speed up future reads.

scenes.headline: Writing partitioned Parquet
scenes.narration: We write the DataFrame in overwrite mode, replacing any existing output. We partition by year and month, which stores the data in a folder structure so later queries filtering on those columns can skip irrelevant files entirely.

scenes.headline: Save modes
scenes.narration: Overwrite replaces existing data and error fails if the path exists, which suit full loads. Append adds new files and ignore skips when data already exists, which fit incremental pipelines.

scenes.text: Partition on columns you frequently filter by, so reads can skip whole folders.
scenes.narration: Choose partition columns you frequently filter on, so future reads can skip entire folders and run much faster.
